{{Quote|Fury Station detected a large incoming object&mdash;something from beyond our system...which then disappeared from ''their'' sensors...|Hawk Ryo|<ref name="DotJ2" />}}
'''Fury Station''' was a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Furies Gate]] in the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] region. The station featured an observatory that could be used to look outward at the rest of the Deep Core, and it was equipped with [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] and communications systems. Fury Station's crew, which numbered at least two, was the sole [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] presence on Furies Gate. The space station was constructed by the settlers of the [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] [[Star system/Legends|system]] several [[Time/Legends|millennia]] before the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[25,793 BBY]], and, over the thousands of years since its establishment, the station was used as a launch point of [[Tythan]] [[Sleeper ship/Legends|sleeper ships]] traveling into the Deep Core.

By 25,793 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], Fury Station was used as a scientific outpost and was run under strict treaty by the [[Settled Worlds]] of the Tython system, with the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gost]] serving as the station's [[Captain/Legends|captain]]. That year, the [[Devourer (Rakatan ship)|''Devourer'']]&mdash;a starship of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]]&mdash;approached Fury Station and was detected by the station's sensors. Unexpectedly, the ''Devourer'' vanished from Fury Station's sensors, and the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Je'daii Ranger]] [[Hawk Ryo]], who was present on the station's bridge at that time, left Fury Station in his [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] to notify the planet of Tython of the situation.

==Description==
Fury Station was a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] Furies Gate&mdash;the outermost [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]] that was located within [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] region.<ref name="DotJ0" /> The station consisted of a rounded central part from which four long modules extended at right angles. In addition, three long components also extended from the lower part of the central module. Fury Station featured a command bridge and at least one [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] capable of housing a [[Hunter-class starfighter|''Hunter''-class starfighter]],<ref name="DotJ2" /> as well as an observatory that could be used to look outward at the rest of the Deep Core.<ref name="DotJ0" /> The [[Realspace/Legends|space]] station was equipped with [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] that were used to monitor the [[Realspace/Legends|space]] for any incoming starships, and communications systems were also installed on the station and were used to send messages to the rest of the [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] [[Star system/Legends|system]] worlds.<ref name="DotJ2" />

By the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[25,793 BBY]],<ref name="CBR" /> Fury Station's crew numbered at least two&mdash;the station's [[Captain/Legends|captain]] and a [[Sensor officer/Legends|sensor officer]]. Nine other individuals were also on the station's bridge that year. The space station's crew wore gray-[[Color/Legends|colored]] uniforms<ref name="DotJ2" /> and were the only [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] presence on the desolate world of Furies Gate.<ref name="DotJ0" />

==History==
{{Quote|Sensors indicate something inbound, Captain Gost. Maybe one of the ''sleeper ships'' has finally found their way home?"''<br />''"A sleeper would ''answer'' our hails.|The station's sensor officer and Gost|<ref name="DotJ2" />}}
[[File:Fury_Station_officers.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The sensor officer and Gost on Fury Station's command bridge]]
Fury Station was constructed by the [[Tythan|settlers]] of the Tython system several [[Time/Legends|millennia]] before<ref name="DotJ2" /> 25,793 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]],<ref name="CBR" /> and, over the thousands of years since its establishment, the station was used as a launch point of Tythan [[Sleeper ship/Legends|sleeper ships]] traveling into the Deep Core, however none of the starships returned to the [[Star/Legends|star]] system.<ref name="DotJ2" /> By 25,793 BBY,<ref name="CBR" /> Fury Station was used as a scientific outpost<ref name="DotJ0" /> and was run under strict treaty by the [[Settled Worlds]] of the Tython system, with the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gost]] serving as the station's captain.<ref name="DotJ2" />

That year, the [[Devourer (Rakatan ship)|''Devourer'']]&mdash;a starship of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]]&mdash;approached Fury Station and was detected by the station's sensors. The space station's [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] [[Unidentified sensor officer (Fury Station)|sensor officer]] notified Gost of the approaching vessel and suggested that a Tythan sleeper ship was finally returning home, however both of them expressed their concern regarding the starship's lack of response to Fury Station's hails and the fact that the vessel's sensor readouts didn't match any of the Tythan starships. Suddenly, the ''Devourer'' vanished from Fury Station's sensors, and Gost ordered the sensor [[Officer/Legends|officer]] to notify the other worlds of the Tython system about the situation. The [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Je'daii Ranger]] [[Hawk Ryo]], who was also present on the station's bridge at that time, then proceeded to Fury Station's hangar where his [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] was docked. From there, Ryo sent a warning message to [[Je'daii Temple Master]] [[Ketu]] on the planet of Tython, and then left the space station for Tython in his fighter.<ref name="DotJ2" />

==Behind the scenes==
Fury Station was first mentioned in ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi 0]]'', a preview issue of the ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi]]'' series of [[Star Wars comic books|comic books]]. The issue was published on [[February 1]], [[2012]], and was written by [[John Ostrander]] and penciled by [[Jan Duursema]]. The space station made its first [[in-universe]] appearance in the [[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 2|second]] issue of the series, published on [[March 21]] of the year 2012.
